message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Molar mass** | 1.008 g mol⁻¹ (protium) |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (¹H), Deuterium (²H), Tritium (³H) |
| **State at STP** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless diatomic gas (H₂) |
| **Density** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (at 0 °C, 1 atm) |
| **Melting point** | –259.1 °C |
| **Boiling point** | –252.8 °C |
| **Ionization energy** | 1312 kJ mol⁻¹ (first ionization) |
| **Electron affinity** | –73 kJ mol⁻¹ (negative, meaning it does not readily accept an electron) |
| **Enthalpy of formation** | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition for elemental H₂) |
| **Standard entropy** | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| **Standard Gibbs free energy of formation** | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| **Heat capacity (Cp)** | 28.84 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 298 K) |
| **Heat capacity (Cv)** | 20.79 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 298 K) |
| **Reactivity** | Highly flammable; reacts with oxygen to form water (combustion). Forms hydrides with metals (e.g., NaH, CaH₂). Can be protonated to form H⁺ (in aqueous solution). |
| **Bonding** | Forms covalent bonds; H₂ is a homonuclear diatomic molecule. In water, participates in hydrogen bonding (though weaker than O–H bonds). |
| **Electrical conductivity** | Poor conductor in neutral state; becomes a good conductor when ionized (plasma). |
| **Applications** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells, rocket propellant), industrial feedstock (ammonia synthesis, methanol production), laboratory reagent, cryogenic coolant (liquid hydrogen). |

**Quick Takeaways**

- Hydrogen is the lightest element, existing naturally as a diatomic gas (H₂).
- It has a very low boiling and melting point, making it gaseous under normal conditions.
- Its ionization energy is high, but its electron affinity is negative, indicating it does not easily accept electrons.
- Hydrogen is highly reactive, especially with oxygen, and is widely used as a clean fuel source and industrial feedstock.
